close_reason: Extended OcspChecker # Limitations to cover delegated responders (RFC 6960 §4.2.2.2), absence of OCSP request generation/nonce, and no AIA-based responder discovery (RFC 6960 §3.1). Cross-referenced pkix-revocation-http for the online story.
description:
pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs:347 (inside parse_and_verify_basic_response):
  // Current limitation: assumes the response is signed directly by the issuer.

This is an important limitation — RFC 6960 §4.2.2.2 delegated OCSP responders (signed by a separate cert with id-kp-OCSPSigning EKU) are not supported. A delegated response will fail with OcspSignatureInvalid because the issuer's SPKI does not verify the response signature.

Fail-closed behaviour is correct (so this is not a security defect). But the limitation belongs in the structured `# Limitations` section of OcspChecker, not as a one-line inline comment. The README's 'Not yet implemented' list (line 150) does mention 'Delegated OCSP responders' so it is acknowledged at the project level, but pkix-revocation's own crate-level docs and OcspChecker docs do not.

Fix: add a 'Limitations' subsection to OcspChecker's docstring (around pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs:35-65) covering:
  - No delegated responder support (RFC 6960 §4.2.2.2)
  - No OCSP request generation (response DER must be supplied; nonce is not checked)
  - No AIA-based responder discovery (RFC 6960 §3.1)

Severity: P4. The behavior is fail-closed and the README mentions it; this is purely doc-discoverability for the rustdoc reader.

Pass-1 attribution: not addressed. Pass 1 P3 commit PKIX-1z05 added doc(cfg(...)) on feature-gated items but didn't restructure limitation prose.
title: P4: pkix-revocation OCSP delegated responder limitation only documented in inline comment, not in # Limitations
